checkpointRows.reviewNotes: The completion-verdict boundary is good, but two compiler labels occupy MasterName and quoted Zhaozhou material may belong to a later raiser. Exact actor ownership is not solved by naming the case's best-known master.

The bowing cloth is properly concrete, but action narration and greetings may be performed by a visitor while the named master is respondent or subject. Eight uniformly named rows need exact grammatical actor review.

The alms-raising office is clear, but compiler and two documentary-narrator labels are MasterName; 'Zonggao' is not roster-exact. Appointment narration, office-holder speech, and record-owner context must be separated.

The reusable interview question is well defined, but the headword is ordinarily uttered by the questioning monk, not the master who answers. All six occurrences are assigned named masters, strongly indicating respondent-as-utterer errors.

The tested-discerner reading is plausible, but commentator, compiler, and two documentary-narrator labels are MasterName values. Questions about a clear-eyed person also belong to their questioner/quoter, not automatically the named subject.
The four guardians' office is bounded, but monastic-rule narrator and assembly speaker are not masters. Canonical narration and immediate address require separate exact-actor branches.

The variable-function gloss is useful, but one documentary narrator is a MasterName and Shakyamuni/Mahakasyapa may be quoted case figures rather than present utterers. Quoter, quoted actor, and subject must be distinguished.

The Shariputra citation-life is appropriately limited, but compiler, lineage narrator, and documentary narrator labels occupy MasterName. The entry must identify exact quoted speakers or narration rather than linking those roles as masters.

The immediate bodily strike is clearly pictured, but the actor can be striker, narrator, visitor, or later commentator. Six universally named rows need proof that each named master actually utters the phrase rather than performs the blow or owns the case.

The physical restraint sense is clear, but Shakyamuni and a hermit may be quoted figures or performers rather than utterers. The all-named pattern needs full-case speaker/action ownership and a different-thing test for literal grasp versus encounter control.
